topic: Filing late vs paying late: the late-filing penalty (ITA 162), what it does not apply to, benefit payments that need a filed return, and the 2026-return deadlines

example.note: example (not a CRA rule): $4,000 of tax unpaid at the filing due date; return 1 filed 4 complete months after April 30, 2027; return 2 filed on time and not paid; return 3 has a refund and is filed late. Interest at the prescribed rate (not stated: it changes quarterly) is not included.

dates.file_business: June 15, 2027 (Tuesday) if you or your cohabiting spouse/common-law partner carried on a business in 2026
dates.balance_due: April 30, 2027 for every individual; interest from May 1

sources.penalty: ITA 162(1): 5% of tax unpaid when the return was required to be filed + 1% of it per complete month late, max 12 months
sources.repeat: ITA 162(2): 10% + 2% per complete month, max 20 months, if a demand to file was sent under 150(2) and a 162(1)/(2) penalty was payable for any of the 3 preceding years
sources.deadlines: ITA 150(1)(d)(i) April 30; 150(1)(d)(ii) June 15 for an individual who carried on a business in the year and their cohabiting spouse/common-law partner
sources.balance_due: ITA 248(1) balance-due day (individual): April 30 of the following year; 161(1) interest at the prescribed rate after it
sources.gst_credit: ITA 122.5(3): the GST/HST credit is deemed paid to an eligible individual who files a return of income for the year
sources.cra: canada.ca late-filing penalty page and CRA tax tips (via search results, 2026-10-13): file on time even if you can't pay; payment arrangements; late filing can interrupt CCB / GST/HST credit payments
